model.name: Commercial Contract
model.purpose: Give agents the context needed to identify, form, read, operate and close a legally binding commercial agreement between two or more parties as a jointly owned record, independent of storage format.
model.scope_statement: Covers the agreement record itself: its identity and classification, the party positions and their authority, how it was concluded and executed, the structure and terms of the agreed text, the obligations and schedule it creates, the record of performance, non-performance, remedy, change, notice and termination, and the governance of that record (provenance, integrity, access, retention, interoperability). Scope is business-to-business commercial contracting, following the HCCH Principles' scope of parties acting in the exercise of their trade or profession. External legal norms, the real-world identity of the parties, procurement award processes and dispute proceedings are referenced, not duplicated.
in_scope: Agreement identity, subject-matter classification and the applicable legal regime declaration
Party positions, their roles, legal identification and signing authority
Formation facts: offer, acceptance, conduct, standard-term incorporation, execution and effectiveness
Addressable clause structure, constituent document set, precedence and authentic language
Commercial terms: price and payment, delivery and risk transfer, warranty, liability and protective terms
Obligations expressed as deontic specifications with bearers, source clauses, violations and reparations
Milestones, due conditions, cure periods and performance/acceptance records
Non-performance, excuse, remedy, amendment, assignment, notice, termination and survival
Record governance: provenance, integrity of the executed text, access, retention, disposition and projections
out_of_scope: Consumer contracts and employment contracts (excluded by the HCCH Principles' commercial scope)
The legal existence, powers and internal governance of the parties themselves (organization/person models)
The procurement or tendering process that precedes award
Conduct of litigation or arbitration proceedings and the resulting awards
Statutory and regulatory norms as such; only their declared applicability to this agreement is in scope
Payment execution, settlement instruments and accounting entries
Transfer of property/title, which CISG Article 4 expressly leaves to the applicable national law
Distributed-ledger execution substrates for smart contracts
Tax determination, transfer pricing and customs classification

boundary_notes.distinction: The tendering, evaluation and award process is owned by the procurement model; UBL separates Tender and Contract Award Notice documents from the resulting contract. Award output composes into a new agreement record here.

The legal entity and its verified identifier (LEI under ISO 17442) live in the party model; this model holds only the party position, its role and the link plus verification evidence. The registry validation flag 'a contract is not an organization' is upheld.

The arbitration or jurisdiction clause, the escalation state and the written-form evidence required by New York Convention Article II are in scope; the proceeding, award and enforcement action are not.

Overriding mandatory rules and statutory regimes (for example CISG applicability, unfair-term controls under the Data Act) are external norms; this model records only the applicability declaration and any opt-out.

Certificate issuance, trusted lists and signature-creation devices belong to the eIDAS trust-service domain; this model records the signature type, assurance level and validation evidence attached to execution.
Specialised agreement types EXTEND this model with domain terms and lifecycle events; their product-specific economics are not duplicated here.

bundle.name: Identity and Legal Frame
bundle.description: What this agreement is, how it is uniquely denoted, what kind of transaction it governs and which law and forum apply to it.

layer.name: Agreement Identity and Classification
layer.description: Denotation of the agreement instance and the coded classification that selects the applicable regime and term expectations.

finding.name: Agreement Record Identity and Instance Boundary
finding.description: How one agreement is distinguished from another, which identifier is authoritative, and where a framework agreement ends and a call-off begins.

questions.text: Which identifier is authoritative for this agreement, who issued it, and is it agreed by all parties?
Does this record denote one binding agreement, or a framework whose obligations arise only on call-off?
answer_data: Instance kind code (standalone, framework, call-off, schedule)

questions.text: How is a specific executed version of this agreement addressed as distinct from the abstract agreement?
If no master-system identifier exists, which Dimension minted the surrogate key and under what authority?

data_elements.name: agreementIdentifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the agreement instance, resolved by the identity priority rule.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Coded scheme of the identifier (master register, governed IRI, or Dimension-minted surrogate).

data_elements.name: parentAgreementRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the framework or master agreement under which this instance is concluded.

artifacts.name: Contract Register Entry
artifacts.description: The authoritative register record asserting the agreement identifier, its scheme, instance kind and links to parent or child instances.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Carries the authoritative master-system identifier where the register is the system of record; otherwise the governed IRI, with any Dimension-minted UUID/ULID recorded as an alias with minting provenance.

layer.name: Party Positions and Legal Identification
layer.description: The roles the agreement creates and the verified real-world entities that occupy them.

finding.name: Party Position and Contractual Role
finding.description: The abstract positions the agreement creates, their roles, and how liability is shared where several parties occupy one side.

questions.text: What role does each party position hold, and from which controlled vocabulary is the role code taken?
answer_data: Position label used in the text

questions.text: Where several obligors occupy one side, are their duties joint, several, or joint and several?
How is a party position kept distinct from the legal entity that currently occupies it?

data_elements.name: partyPositionId
data_elements.description: Identifier of a position in the agreement, stable across changes of the occupying entity.

data_elements.name: partyRoleCode
data_elements.description: Coded contractual role such as buyer, seller, licensor, supplier, guarantor.

data_elements.name: obligorPluralityMode
data_elements.description: How liability is shared among several obligors on the same side.

finding.inline_only_rationale: A party position is a structural slot in the agreement record, not a document. Its evidence is the executed text and the identity verification record held by the neighbouring finding; creating an artifact for a slot would assert a document that does not exist.

finding.name: Legal Identification and Place of Business
finding.description: The governed identifier for each party, the verification evidence behind it, and the place of business that drives regime applicability.

questions.text: Which governed global identifier denotes each party, and what is its current registration status?
What is each party's relevant place of business, and how was it determined where several exist?
What evidence supports the link between the named party in the text and the identified legal entity?
How is a party's change of name, registration or legal form recorded without breaking the position link?

data_elements.description: Twenty-character governed identifier of the legal entity occupying a party position, where available.

data_elements.name: placeOfBusiness
data_elements.description: Party's relevant place of business, used to determine uniform-regime applicability and communication rules.

data_elements.name: identityVerificationTime
data_elements.description: Observation time at which the party identity was last verified against the authoritative registry.

artifacts.name: Party Identity Verification Record
artifacts.description: Dated record of the check that ties the party named in the text to a registry entry, capturing method, source, result and verifier.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by party position identifier plus a zero-padded verification sequence number scoped to that position; carries the verified legal entity identifier as a foreign key.

layer.name: Authority and Representation
layer.description: The power of the individuals and intermediaries who bind the parties, and the positions of third parties who are affected without signing.

finding.name: Signing Authority and Capacity
finding.description: Who executed the agreement for each party, on what basis they were empowered, and what limits bounded that power.

questions.text: On what basis was each signatory empowered to bind the party, and where is that basis recorded?
What monetary, subject-matter or duration limits bound the signatory's authority at execution time?
If authority was exceeded, is the agreement treated as ratified, void, or binding on apparent authority?
Was signing authority verified before execution, by whom, and at what observation time?

data_elements.name: signingAuthorityBasis
data_elements.description: Coded basis of the signatory's power (statutory representative, board resolution, power of attorney, delegated mandate).

data_elements.name: authorityLimitAmount
data_elements.description: Monetary ceiling on the signatory's power, with its currency code.

artifacts.name: Authority Evidence Instrument
artifacts.description: The power of attorney, board resolution, register extract or delegation record relied on to show the signatory could bind the party.

bundle.description: How the agreement came into existence, how consent was expressed and evidenced, and when it began to bite.

layer.name: Consent and Conclusion
layer.description: The offer, acceptance or conduct that concluded the agreement, and whose standard terms became part of it.

finding.name: Offer, Acceptance and Incorporated Standard Terms
finding.description: The communications and conduct that concluded the contract, when and where they took effect, and which standard terms were incorporated when both sides sent their own.

questions.text: By what act was the contract concluded: acceptance of a definite offer, conduct indicating assent, or an automated exchange?
At what dispatch and receipt times did the concluding communication take effect, in each party's offset?
Whose standard terms were incorporated, and how was a conflict between competing form sets resolved?
Was the proposal sufficiently definite as to goods, quantity and price for a binding contract to arise?

data_elements.name: conclusionMode
data_elements.description: Coded manner in which assent was expressed (signed instrument, offer and acceptance, conduct, automated system).

data_elements.name: conclusionEventTime
data_elements.description: Time at which the contract was concluded, recorded with seconds and explicit offset.

data_elements.name: incorporatedTermSetRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a standard term set incorporated by reference, with its version and the incorporation clause.

artifacts.name: Formation Communication Set
artifacts.description: The ordered set of pre-contractual communications (quotation, purchase order, order confirmation, acceptance message) relied on to show conclusion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each communication keyed by its transport message identifier where one exists, otherwise by a Dimension-minted ULID; ordered by a zero-padded sequence scoped to the agreement identifier.

layer.description: The signature or seal evidence attached to the agreed text, and the conditions that had to be met before it took effect.

finding.name: Execution, Signature Type and Form Requirement
finding.description: How the agreement was signed or sealed, the assurance level and validation evidence of that signature, and any form requirement it had to satisfy.

questions.text: Does any applicable rule require this agreement or a clause within it to be in writing or signed?
What signature or seal type was used by each signatory, and at what assurance level?
What validation evidence proves the signature was valid at signing time and remains verifiable now?
When and in which offset did each party execute, and which execution completed the agreement?

data_elements.name: executionTime
data_elements.description: Time at which a signatory executed, with seconds and the local offset of the place of execution preserved.

data_elements.name: signatureType
data_elements.description: Coded signature or seal type and its assurance level under the applicable trust framework.

data_elements.name: signedDataDigest
data_elements.description: Digest over the exact bytes covered by each signature, with the algorithm identifier.

artifacts.name: Signature Evidence Package
artifacts.description: The signed container, certificates, time-stamp tokens and validation report that together evidence execution and allow later re-verification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus signatory position and a zero-padded signature sequence; content-addressed by the digest of the signed bytes.

layer.name: Execution and Effectiveness
layer.description: The signature or seal evidence attached to the agreed text, and the conditions that had to be met before it took effect.

finding.name: Conditions Precedent, Effectiveness and Validity Defects
finding.description: The gap between execution and effect: conditions to be satisfied, approvals to be obtained, and defects that can unwind consent.

questions.text: Which conditions had to be satisfied or waived before obligations became enforceable, and what is each one's status?
How does the effective date differ from the execution date, and does any term apply retroactively?
Is any ground of invalidity asserted, such as mistake, fraud, threat or gross disparity, and by whom?
If a term is invalid or unenforceable, does the remainder of the agreement survive?

data_elements.name: effectiveDate
data_elements.description: Date or timestamp from which the agreement's obligations take effect.

data_elements.name: conditionPrecedent
data_elements.description: A condition to be satisfied or waived before effectiveness, with its status and evidence.

data_elements.name: validityStatus
data_elements.description: Current validity state of the agreement (effective, conditional, avoided, disputed).

finding.inline_only_rationale: Effectiveness is a computed state over conditions, clauses and events already held elsewhere; the documents that satisfy a condition (a regulatory approval, a guarantee) are artifacts owned by their own models or by the notice finding. bundle.name: Agreed Text and Commercial Terms

layer.name: Document Structure and Precedence
layer.description: How provisions are addressed, which documents constitute the contract, how conflicts between them resolve, and which language governs.

finding.name: Clause Addressability and Structure
finding.description: Stable identification of individual provisions across versions, their classification and their machine-readable form.

questions.text: How is a single provision addressed so the reference survives renumbering in a later amended version?
What functional class does a provision belong to, and which classification scheme assigns it?
What digest fixes the exact wording of a provision as executed?
Which machine-readable rule, if any, is asserted to represent this provision, and who asserted it?

data_elements.name: clauseExpressionId
data_elements.description: Expression-level identifier of a provision, valid within one version of the text.

data_elements.name: clauseWorkId
data_elements.description: Work-level identifier that persists across expressions, allowing a provision to be tracked through amendments.

data_elements.name: clauseClass
data_elements.description: Coded functional class of the provision (payment, liability, termination, confidentiality, governing law).

artifacts.name: Clause Tree Expression
artifacts.description: The hierarchical, addressable representation of one version of the agreed text with per-node identifiers and digests.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the FRBR expression IRI of the agreed text; each node addressed by its expression identifier, with the persistent work identifier retained for cross-version tracking.

finding.description: Each duty expressed with its deontic type, bearer, auxiliary party, source clause and the violation and reparation that follow non-compliance.

questions.text: Is this norm an obligation, a permission, a prohibition or a right, and who bears it?
Which provision creates this duty, and does any other provision qualify or defeat it?
What counts as violation of this duty, and what penalty or reparation is chained to it?
What is the current state of the duty: not yet due, due, performed, waived, or violated?

data_elements.name: deonticType

data_elements.name: obligationStatus

questions.text: Is the duty triggered by a fixed date, an elapsed period, or the occurrence of another event?
How long is any grace or cure period, and from which notice or event does it run?
Is timely performance treated as essential, so that delay alone justifies avoidance?
Which milestones depend on the completion of others, and what happens when an upstream one slips?

Against which agreed metric was performance measured, and what value was observed?
Did the counterparty accept, reject or accept with reservations, and within what period?

functions.name: Register agreement record
functions.description: Create the jointly owned record for a new agreement with its identifier, party positions, classification and legal frame.
inputs: Party position set with role codes
preconditions: At least two party positions are declared
A commercial-scope assertion exists for every position
Governing law and forum are declared or explicitly marked absent
effects: Agreement identifier is bound and cannot be reassigned
Record enters the pre-effective state
Registration event is written to the audit log with event and ingestion time

functions.name: Verify party identity and signing authority
functions.description: Check each named party against the authoritative registry and confirm the signatory's power to bind within its limits.
preconditions: A party position exists
An authority basis is asserted
effects: Verification observation time is recorded
Authority defect raises an exception state instead of blocking silently

functions.name: Record conclusion and execution
functions.description: Capture the concluding communications or signatures, the effective moment and the signature validation evidence.
inputs: Formation communication set or signed container
preconditions: Party identity and authority verification have been attempted and their results recorded
Any applicable form requirement has been identified
effects: Executed expression digest is fixed and becomes immutable
Record moves to conditional or effective state depending on outstanding conditions

functions.name: Build addressable clause tree
functions.description: Convert the agreed text into a hierarchy of addressable provisions with expression and work identifiers and per-node digests.
preconditions: The manifestation's digest matches the executed expression digest
effects: Clause references become stable across later amendments
Any extraction uncertainty is recorded as provenance, not silently normalised

functions.name: Derive obligation set
functions.description: Produce deontic statements with bearers, conditions, violations and reparations traced to source clauses.
preconditions: Clause tree exists with stable identifiers
Bearer positions are resolvable
effects: Derived rules are marked as derived, never as the normative text
A later amendment invalidates and re-derives the affected rules

functions.name: Evaluate effectiveness and conditions
functions.description: Determine whether conditions precedent are satisfied or waived and compute the current validity state.
preconditions: Execution has been recorded
Each condition has an evidence slot
effects: Obligations become enforceable only after the effectiveness event
Lapse at long-stop date is recorded as an event, not a deletion

functions.name: Monitor due obligations
functions.description: Compute which duties are due, overdue or within a cure period from due conditions and recorded events.
preconditions: Obligations carry due conditions
All timestamps carry seconds and explicit offsets
effects: Status transitions are emitted as events with event and observation time
No status is inferred without an evidenced trigger

functions.name: Record performance and acceptance
functions.description: Attach evidence that a duty was performed, capture measured results and register the counterparty's acceptance decision.
preconditions: The obligation exists and is due or performable
The recording actor is authorised for that party position
effects: Event time and observation time are stored separately
Deemed acceptance is applied only where an agreed rule exists

functions.name: Declare non-performance and elect remedy
functions.description: Register a breach declaration, any asserted excuse, the remedy elected and its quantification.
preconditions: A notice satisfying the contractual notice rules has been issued where required
Any cure period has expired or is expressly waived
effects: Record enters a disputed state that blocks disposition
Remedy election is immutable once notified, subject to a superseding agreed settlement

functions.name: Apply executed amendment

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate and both explicitly uphold the registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization. The boundary is the jointly owned multi-party agreement record composed of party positions, clause structure, deontic obligations and lifecycle events, with the legal entities, the procurement award process, adjudication proceedings, proprietary/title effects, insolvency and settlement execution held as neighbouring models. Claude's six sourced boundary notes and grok's CISG/HCCH sphere-of-application notes agree on every exclusion, so the boundary is settled before any node is accepted.

decisions.rationale: Claude has six sourced boundary notes naming concrete neighbour models, an explicit inline_only_rationale for every finding that mints no artifact, a sixteen-dimension coverage checklist with no self-declared gap, and separate findings for provenance, access, retention and interoperability. Grok is stronger on CISG article-level depth but declares a validation gap and lumps notices, dispute clauses, joint record, access and retention into one composite finding, which is the less clear boundary.

model.name: Obligation / Commitment
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral structure for a directed deontic commitment: which party owes which action or forbearance, to whom, under which conditions, by when, to what standard, how it is discharged, and what follows if it is not.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-029 models a single obligation/commitment instance as a mixin that can be attached to any host record that creates or carries duties (contract clause, statute or regulation article, licence, court or administrative order, service commitment, internal policy, unilateral promise). It covers the deontic core (bearer, counterparty, modality, action), the conditional structure that detaches the duty, the temporal structure (due time, recurrence, grace, limitation), the lifecycle state model, fulfilment and its evidence, non-performance with excuse and remedy, the authority and provenance that make the duty defensible, and transfer, plurality and standards alignment. It deliberately does not model the instrument, the parties, the executed work or the accounting recognition; those are referenced from sibling models.

boundary_notes.distinction: An agreement is a negotiated understanding reflecting offer and acceptance of commitments; a commitment is a promise by one party to act or refrain. One agreement carries many obligations, and an obligation can exist with no agreement at all (statute, court order, unilateral commitment, commitment at large). This model references the instrument and never restates its terms.

ODRL places Duties inside a Policy, either as a policy-level obligation or as a pre-condition duty on a Permission. This mixin sits at the Rule/Duty level, not the container level; the policy grouping, conflict strategy and inheritance belong to the policy model.

A right is the reciprocal aspect of a commitment and is borne by a different party; LegalRuleML models a Right as a permission to a bearer that implies obligations on auxiliary parties. The correlative right is referenced, not duplicated, so that assignment of the right and transfer of the duty stay separable.

A prohibition is violated by performing the act, an obligation by failing to perform it. The modality and violation polarity are recorded here, but negative-duty enforcement semantics (remedy on infringement) differ from consequence semantics on unfulfilled duties and must not be collapsed.

A task is an execution artefact. Several tasks may contribute to discharging one obligation, and tasks exist with no obligation behind them. Progress measurement is carried here only as a discharge measure, not as work scheduling.

IFRS 15 performance obligations are only promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer; obligations outside that definition fall to other standards. Recognition, measurement and presentation of the financial effect are out of scope and belong to a financial-reporting model.

ODRL defines Constraint as leftOperand/operator/rightOperand and LogicalConstraint as and/or/xone/andSequence. This model references those expression structures and their operand vocabularies rather than redefining operators.

A compliance management system maintains a register of obligations the organisation must or voluntarily chooses to meet. That register is a collection-level and programme-level concern; this model describes one obligation entry and does not carry control design or assurance results.

SBVR separates alethic necessities, which cannot be violated even in principle, from deontic obligations, which may be violated although they ought not to be. Structural necessities must not be represented as obligations in this model.

PROV-O supplies the entity/activity/agent vocabulary for how the obligation record came to be. This model aligns to it and carries the minimum provenance fields inline; the full provenance graph belongs to the provenance model.

finding.name: Obligation identity, versioning and occurrence distinction
finding.description: An obligation record needs a stable identity that survives amendment, is distinct from the clause or article that created it, and is distinct from each dated occurrence of a recurring duty. finding.name: Antecedent condition, detachment and interference
finding.description: Most commitments are conditional: the duty exists but only becomes due when its antecedent holds. UNIDROIT distinguishes a suspensive condition, which delays effect, from a resolutive condition, which terminates it, imposes a duty to preserve the other party's rights while the condition is pending, and makes improper interference with the occurrence of a condition actionable. ODRL expresses the equivalent gate as constraints that must all be satisfied. Detachment is an observable event and must be timestamped and attributable.

finding.name: Obligation states, transitions and dual timestamps
finding.description: An obligation moves through states that must be explicit rather than inferred: proposed, active but conditional, detached and due, in performance, partly fulfilled, fulfilled or discharged, breached, excused, waived or released, cancelled, transferred, expired and superseded. ODRL derives fulfilment from constraint satisfaction plus exercise of the refined action, and treats a duty as unfulfilled unless its consequences are also fulfilled; LegalRuleML makes Violation and Compliance explicit indications. Every transition needs both the instant the change legally took effect and the instant the system observed or ingested it, because these routinely differ for externally evidenced events. finding.description: ODRL states that a duty is fulfilled if all its constraints are satisfied and its action, with all refinements satisfied, has been exercised, and that where the action has not been exercised all consequences must be fulfilled instead. IFRS 15 ties satisfaction to transfer of control, either over time or at a point in time. Acceptance by the obligee is a separate step from performance and must not be conflated with it; discharge can also occur by substitute performance, set-off, waiver or release, each of which is a different discharge mode with different evidential needs.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently arrived at mixin, and the base scope statement, ten boundary notes and explicit out-of-scope list draw complete lines against the agreement instrument, party master data, the policy/rule container, task execution, payment and settlement mechanics, dispute management, control registers and accounting recognition. The base also passes the definitional/alethic filter (SBVR) that keeps non-violable necessities out of the register. The only boundary pressure in this adjudication is the imported access-control and conformance obligation sense, which is admitted as a crosswalk alignment entry only, leaving the base exclusion of decision-point and evaluation infrastructure intact.

decisions.rationale: The base carries ten boundary notes, an explicit out-of-scope list and adversarial counterexamples (commitment at large, negative duty, asset-free statutory duty, maintenance duty, owed-but-time-barred duty) that close the model edges. The alternative's seven notes are sound but leave party roles, stewardship, provenance and retention thin. Node count was not decisive; edge completeness was.

Both providers independently classified the entry as a mixin attachable to contracts, statutes, licences, orders, policies and unilateral commitments, and neither structure carries instrument formation, party identity or ledger semantics that would force a standalone entity.

Tier-1 primary grounding for two obligation homonyms absent from the base crosswalk; admitted as mapping and sense-disambiguation only, with the source finding's access and retention material dropped as duplicative of base access-and-retention.

decisions.concept: IAS 37 provision recognition and measurement overlay
decisions.rationale: The base explicitly out-of-scopes accounting recognition and measurement and draws a boundary note to Liability/Provision. Importing provision amount, risk adjustment, discounting and onerous-contract testing would reopen a deliberately closed edge and duplicate a sibling financial-reporting model.

decisions.concept: IAS 37 legal versus constructive obligation classification
decisions.rationale: Adjacent to but not identical with the base external-versus-voluntary origin axis from ISO 37301. Deciding whether constructive obligation is an origin class of the duty or only a recognition trigger requires primary clause text neither provider read, so it is not bolted onto obligation-typology on inference.

Tier-3 non-primary profile, and the source provider itself flags adopting it as canonical as an over-claim. The base lifecycle-state-machine is grounded in the ODRL fulfilment test, LegalRuleML Violation/Compliance indications and the achievement/maintenance distinction, which is stronger support.

Place and currency of performance already sit in base subject-and-place, and ordering with reciprocal dependency in finding-composition-and-dependency; importing the finding would fragment place of performance across two nodes. Its one unique element, withholding performance, is deferred to research instead.

Base antecedent-and-detachment plus constraint-expression already carry suspensive and resolutive conditions, detachment evidence and timestamping, improper interference, and the full ODRL Constraint and LogicalConstraint expression form including andSequence ordering.
